description.description: Clear, concise user-facing description of the update you are waiting for. This may be shown directly in chat, so make it grammatical by itself. Describe the expected event, not the polling command or monitor implementation. Prefer `CI results and review comments for the auth fix`, `Deployment completion or failure`, or `New errors in the API logs` over internal labels like `PR checks and state transitions`.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms, max 3600000ms. Ignored when persistent is true.

persistent.description: Run for the lifetime of the session (no timeout). Use for session-length watches like PR monitoring or log tails. Stop with TaskStop.

backup_after_seconds.description: Optional backup: if the monitor emits nothing for this many seconds (from start or its last event), a durable Wake fires in this conversation so a stalled watch can't go silent. Each event resets the clock; the backup is cancelled when the monitor ends or is stopped. Survives restarts of this process.

backup_prompt.description: Instruction for the backup wake's turn. Defaults to checking the real state of what the monitor watches, then reporting, re-arming, or stopping it.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
